body:
Balance and Undo (lesson)
1. x = 14 (subtract 9).
2. x = 9 (divide by 5).
3. 2x = 14, x = 7. Check: 2(7) + 3 = 17.
4. x/4 = 5, x = 20. Check: 20 ÷ 4 - 2 = 3.
5. The equation multiplies x by 3 and then adds 6, so we undo in reverse order: first subtract 6, then divide by 3. 3x = 15, x = 5.

Two-Step Equations in Context
1. 4x = 28, x = 7.
2. 25 + 15m = 130; 15m = 105; m = 7 months.
3. 2(15) + 2w = 54; 30 + 2w = 54; 2w = 24; w = 12 cm.

Equivalent Expressions
1. 8x - 12.
2. 3(2x + 5).
3. 2x + 9.
4. 4y - 3 + 3y = 7y - 3.
5. p - 0.2p shows the original price minus the 20% discount; 0.8p shows the shopper pays 80% of the price. They are equal because p - 0.2p = (1 - 0.2)p = 0.8p.
6. 2(x + 4) + 2(3) and 2x + 14 (or x + 4 + 3 + x + 4 + 3). 2(x + 4) + 6 = 2x + 8 + 6 = 2x + 14.

Equations and Inequalities Check (assessment)
1. 6x = 36, x = 6.
2. 0.5x = 7, x = 14.
3. x + 5 = 18, x = 13 (or 2x + 10 = 36, 2x = 26, x = 13).
4. 8 + 3h = 26; 3h = 18; h = 6 hours.
5. 12 + 4n ≤ 40; 4n ≤ 28; n ≤ 7. He can buy 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6 or 7 notebooks: whole numbers only.
6. 3x > 15, x > 5. An open circle at 5 with the ray shaded to the right.
7. Dividing by 4 must divide every term: 4x ÷ 4 + 8 ÷ 4 = 32 ÷ 4 gives x + 2 = 8, so x = 6. (Or subtract 8 first: 4x = 24, x = 6.) Check: 4(6) + 8 = 32.

Scoring tip: score the equation criterion on whether the equation matches the story, even if the solving has a slip. On problem 5, Advanced work states that only whole numbers from 0 to 7 make sense; n ≤ 7 alone is Proficient.
title: Answer key: Unit 3: Equations
